t4.descripcion:
Knowing the customs and typical expressions will help you integrate better:
• "Apuntes": class notes. It is common to share them with classmates.
• "Trabajo en grupo": collaborative task. Participation is highly valued.
• "Examen parcial" and "examen final": assessments throughout the course.
• "Convocatoria": official exam period. There are two exam sessions per year.
• "Suspender" and "aprobar": suspender means to fail; aprobar means to pass.
• "Nota de corte": minimum grade to enter a degree program.
• "Beca": financial aid for students.
• "Erasmus": European exchange program.
• "Tutor": teacher who guides students.
• "Decano": highest authority of a faculty.

📌 IMPORTANT NOTE: In Spain, it is common for students to organize study groups and share notes. Don't be afraid to ask your classmates for help.

❌ COMMON MISTAKE: Chinese students often translate "examen" as "考试" and "prueba" also as "考试", but in Spanish "prueba" can be a short exam or a practical assessment; "examen" is more formal. Also, "nota" is used for grades, not "grado" (which is a degree).
ejemplos: ¿Me puedes prestar los apuntes de la clase de hoy?
El trabajo en grupo cuenta un 30% de la nota final.
La primera convocatoria de exámenes es en enero.
He solicitado una beca para el próximo curso.
El tutor nos ayuda a organizar el estudio.

t2.descripcion:
University life in Spain offers many services and activities. It is important to know them:
• Facultad: building where your degree is taught. Each faculty has its own secretariat and dean's office.
• Aula: classroom. It can be theoretical or practical (laboratory).
• Horario: normally classes are in the morning or afternoon. It is common to have 50-minute classes.
• Tutorías: consultation hours with the professor. You can ask academic questions.
• Biblioteca: book lending, study rooms and access to databases.
• Campus virtual: online platform where you will find notes, assignments and grades.
• Comedor universitario: affordable menu for students.
• Asociaciones de estudiantes: cultural and sports activities.

📌 IMPORTANT NOTE: In Spain, it is common to use "tú" with professors at university, but on first contact it is better to use "usted" until they invite you to use "tú".

❌ COMMON ERROR: Chinese students tend to call all teachers "profesor", but in Spain "profesor" is used for the teacher and "maestro" only for primary education. Also, you should not say "asistir a la universidad" to refer to going to class; you say "ir a clase" or "asistir a clase".
ejemplos: La facultad de Filosofía y Letras está en el centro.
Tengo tutoría con el profesor de Historia mañana a las diez.
En la biblioteca puedes estudiar hasta las nueve de la noche.
El comedor universitario ofrece menú por 5 euros.
Consulta el campus virtual para descargar los apuntes.

t3.descripcion:
Finding accommodation is one of the biggest challenges for international students. Here are some tips and vocabulary:
• Piso compartido: you rent a room in a flat with other students. It is the most common option.
• Residencia de estudiantes: room with full board or half board. It is usually more expensive but more convenient.
• Contrato de alquiler: legal document that you must sign. Read the conditions carefully (fianza, gastos incluidos, duración).
• Fianza: security deposit that is usually one month's rent.
• Gastos incluidos: water, electricity, gas and internet. Ask if they are included in the price.
• Agencia inmobiliaria: intermediary that charges a commission.
• Anuncios: websites like Idealista or Fotocasa to look for a flat.
• Convivencia: house rules (cleaning, noise, visitors).

📌 IMPORTANT NOTE: Never pay a fianza without having seen the flat and signed a contract. Be wary of offers that are too cheap.

❌ COMMON MISTAKE: Chinese students sometimes say "alquilar un piso" when they are only renting a room. In Spanish, "alquilar un piso" means renting the entire flat. For a room, you say "alquilar una habitación" or "compartir piso".
ejemplos: Busco una habitación en un piso compartido cerca de la universidad.
La fianza es de un mes y los gastos están incluidos.
He visto un anuncio en Idealista para compartir piso.
Antes de firmar el contrato, lee bien las normas de convivencia.
La residencia de estudiantes incluye desayuno y cena.

t1.descripcion:
To study in Spain you need to complete several administrative procedures. Here are the most important ones:
• Matrícula: official enrollment at the university. It is done at the registrar's office or online.
• Documentación: passport, student visa, admission letter, health insurance and proof of accommodation.
• NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjero): it is mandatory for stays longer than three months. It is requested at the Oficina de Extranjería.
• Empadronamiento: registration at the town hall of the municipality where you live.
• Tarjeta sanitaria: some students can apply for it; others must take out private insurance.
• Homologación de títulos: official recognition of your previous studies.
• Cuenta bancaria: many universities and scholarships require a Spanish bank account.

📌 IMPORTANT NOTE: The NIE is an essential document for opening a bank account, signing a rental contract or enrolling. Request it as soon as possible.

❌ COMMON MISTAKE: Chinese students often confuse "matrícula" with "inscripción". In Spain, "matrícula" is used for university and "inscripción" for short courses or activities. Also, it should not be confused with "matrícula" for a car (license plate).
ejemplos: Tengo que hacer la matrícula en la universidad antes del 30 de septiembre.
Para solicitar el NIE, necesitas el pasaporte y la carta de admisión.
El empadronamiento se hace en el ayuntamiento de tu ciudad.
He solicitado la homologación de mi título de bachillerato.
Muchos estudiantes abren una cuenta bancaria para pagar la matrícula.
